title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
keyIdea: Slide a window [left, right] that never contains a repeat, with its characters in a set. Move right one step at a time; if s[right] is already inside, erase from the left until it isn't. Each character enters and leaves the window once: O(n).

approaches.name: Brute force: every start
approaches.idea: For each start i, extend j with a fresh set until a repeat appears; track the longest.
approaches.why: Each start can scan up to k characters (k = alphabet / longest answer), so up to O(n²) on long strings.

approaches.name: Sliding window + set
approaches.idea: For each right: while s[right] is in the window, erase s[left] and left++. Then insert s[right] and update maxi with right − left + 1.
approaches.why: right moves n times and left moves at most n times in total; set operations are O(1).

quiz.q: Why a while (not an if) when shrinking?
options: The old copy of s[right] may be several characters in, and everything up to it must leave

quiz.q: Why is it O(n) with a loop inside a loop?
options: left only moves forward, so all the inner loops together erase at most n characters
